_about: Flown failures with a published cause, and the marsflight mechanism that reproduces each. 'confidence': opened = read in the source; excerpt = read in a quoted passage of it; secondary = a news report quoting the source. 'replica' names the test in task/dev/test_failures.py, or the existing mechanism, or 'not modeled'.

failures.name: Mars Polar Lander
failures.cause: A Hall-effect touchdown sensor gave a spurious signal when the legs deployed at about 1,500 m. The software latched it; when touchdown sensing was enabled at 40 m the engines were cut, and the lander fell at about 22 m/s.
failures.source: JPL Special Review Board, JPL D-18709 (Mar 22, 2000), https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20000061966/downloads/20000061966.pdf
failures.design_against: flight software that ignores the sensors until enabled and needs two readings in a row (fault_protection.py)

failures.name: ExoMars Schiaparelli
failures.cause: The IMU saturated after parachute inflation for about 1 s. The software integrated the saturated rate into an attitude error of about 165 deg, the radar ranges then gave a negative altitude, and the parachute was released and the thrusters stopped after 3 s. Free fall from about 3.7 km.
failures.source: ESA ExoMars 2016 Schiaparelli Anomaly Inquiry, DG-I/2017/546/TTN (May 18, 2017), pp.11-12, https://sci.esa.int/documents/33431/35950/1567260317467-ESA_ExoMars_2016_Schiaparelli_Anomaly_Inquiry.pdf; duration: ESA update Nov 23, 2016
failures.design_against: a plausibility check on the height, a test of saturation handling

failures.name: Genesis
failures.cause: The deceleration-sensing G-switches were drawn inverted relative to the Stardust heritage design and built to the drawing. They never sensed entry, so the drogue never fired. Impact at about 311 km/h.
failures.design_against: a centrifuge test of the sequencer

failures.name: Proton-M / GLONASS
failures.cause: All three yaw-channel angular rate sensors were installed 180 deg wrong. The vehicle crashed at about 32.7 s. The polarity check had been dropped from the mandatory list in 2011.
failures.source: Roscosmos board statement, Jul 18, 2013; Rogozin, Sep 16, 2013, http://government.ru/en/news/5806/

failures.name: Vega VV17
failures.cause: Cables to the AVUM thrust vector actuators were swapped during integration, so steering commands were reversed.

failures.name: Ariane 5 flight 501
failures.cause: A horizontal velocity variable in alignment software reused from Ariane 4 overflowed in both inertial reference units (backup at 36.7 s, active 0.05 s later). The on-board computer read diagnostic data as flight data and drove the nozzles hard over; the vehicle broke up at 39 s. Redundancy did not help: both units ran the same software.
failures.design_against: requalify reused software on this vehicle's trajectory

failures.name: Falcon 9 CRS-7
failures.cause: A strut holding a helium bottle (COPV) inside the second stage LOX tank broke near 3.2 g at about 139 s; it was certified for 10,000 lbf and failed at about 2,000 lbf. The bottle broke free and the tank overpressured. NASA's IRT names a cast industrial-grade rod end and calls it a design error.
failures.source: SpaceX CRS-7 investigation update (Jul 20, 2015) via https://www.spacex.com/launches/crs7 and NASASpaceflight (Jul 20, 2015); NASA IRT public summary (Mar 12, 2018), https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/public_summary_nasa_irt_spacex_crs-7_final.pdf

failures.name: Mars Climate Orbiter
failures.cause: The ground software SM_FORCES wrote angular momentum desaturation impulses in lbf s instead of N s, so small-force delta-v was underestimated by a factor of 4.45 and the orbiter arrived far lower than navigation believed.
failures.source: MCO Mishap Investigation Board Phase I report (Nov 10, 1999), https://llis.nasa.gov/llis_lib/pdf/1009464main1_0641-mr.pdf
failures.design_against: an end-to-end test of the navigation data chain
failures.replica: unit check in test_failures (bias in obs); a flown replica needs a Mars approach with targeting

failures.name: Phobos-Grunt
failures.cause: Both halves of the TsVM22 computer restarted, most likely from heavy charged particles hitting RAM chips that were not space-qualified; the spacecraft stayed in safe mode and never left Earth orbit.
failures.design_against: radiation-tested parts; flight software that restarts the computer (restart:<id>)
failures.replica: mechanism in flown.py; flown in test_failures only through the descent stand-in

failures.name: Taurus XL / OCO and Glory
failures.cause: The fairing did not separate and the vehicle could not reach orbit with its mass. For Glory a side rail did not fracture; in 2019 NASA found the extrusion supplier had falsified test results.
failures.source: OCO MIB summary (Jul 2009), https://nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/369037main_ocoexecutivesummary_71609.pdf; Glory MIB summary (Feb 2013), https://www.nasa.gov/pdf/728836main_T9_MIB_Public_Release_Summary.pdf
failures.design_against: a second pyro initiator covers initiation failures only; a mechanism failure is not covered
failures.program_test: none new (rates from Chang and Bement)

failures.name: Antares Orb-3
failures.cause: An AJ26 LOX turbopump exploded after rubbing in the hydraulic balance assembly seal; credible root causes were weak design margin, debris or a machining defect.
failures.mode: program.py engine reliability (hidden reliability factor) and the turbopump model
failures.replica: existing mechanism; turbopump physics is the turbopump model

failures.name: H-II F5
failures.cause: During the second burn a brazed joint below the LE-5A throat partly failed, hot gas leaked, melted control wiring and the engine stopped early.

failures.name: Falcon 1 flight 3
failures.cause: The regeneratively cooled Merlin 1C kept a small thrust after cutoff; the first stage hit the second after separation.

failures.name: Falcon 1 flight 2
failures.cause: Second stage LOX slosh coupled with thrust vector control (no baffles); roll and early shutdown.

failures.name: Apollo 13 / AS-508
failures.cause: S-II pogo oscillations at 14 to 16 Hz shut the center engine down 132 s early; the outboard engines ran 34.5 s longer and orbit was reached.
failures.source: MSFC Saturn V Flight Evaluation Trend Report AS-501 to 508, Tables 2 and 15, https://www.ibiblio.org/apollo/Documents/Saturn_V_Flight_Evaluation_Trend_Report_AS-501_thru_508.pdf

failures.name: Mars Observer
failures.cause: Most probably a rupture of the fuel (MMH) pressurization side of the propulsion system during tank pressurization before orbit insertion.

failures.name: Beresheet
failures.cause: A command to fix a faulty IMU set off a computer reset chain that shut the main engine down; restarts failed.
failures.source: SpaceIL statements via Times of Israel, https://www.timesofisrael.com/5-6-attempts-to-restart-israeli-moon-landers-engine-failed-investigation-finds/
failures.replica: test_avionics_string (dual string without fault protection crashes)

failures.name: HAKUTO-R M1
failures.cause: Crossing a crater rim made the laser rangefinder altitude jump; the software rejected valid readings, believed it was at zero altitude about 5 km up, and ran out of propellant.
failures.mode: not modeled yet (terrain jump against flight software filter)
